findings.what: The opponent's (player-2 'Goldfish') hand is rendered face-up to player-1 (Seal of Discord, Chemtech Enforcer readable at top of board; all 6 face-up by step 40), and the client-side state given to player-1 contains the full identities of player-2's hand cards (handIds/hand[] include player-2-main-37-ogn-204-298, player-2-main-0-ogn-003-298, player-2-main-17-ven-007-166, player-2-main-32-ogn-179-298).
findings.why_wrong: Rule 108.7.c / 128.4: cards in a player's hand are Private Information — only the owner may look at them; 129.3: hand cards present their back side. DESIGN.md lists no Goldfish-mode exception. If this is an intentional solo-mode reveal it should be UI-only; the server shipping opponent hand contents in the player-scoped state is a hidden-information leak that would carry over to Host/Join games.
findings.reason: Server leak confirmed. buildGameSnapshot (apps/riftbound-app/server.ts:638-719) iterates every zone in internal.zones — including the shared "hand" zone — and emits id/definitionId/name/rulesText for every card regardless of owner (lines 659-693); its `viewingPlayer` parameter is never used. The same unfiltered snapshot is then sent to every connected client on every move (server.ts:3040 built once, sent to actor at 3051-3060 and to all other clients at 3063-3076; also resync at 3091-3099, pregame broadcast 1242-1253, game start 2930-2941) with no `session.sandbox` gating, so opponent hand identities are shipped to the other player in Host/Join games too, violating rules 108.7.c/128.4 (hand is Private Information). The face-up UI render itself is an intentional goldfish-only client choice (public/js/gameplay/renderer.js:729-732 gates on isSandboxGame, otherwise renders card backs), but that is UI-only masking over a server payload that already contains the full opponent hand.

findings.what: Playing Patched Porobot (player controls zero gear — base was empty, no equipment/gear anywhere on their board) put a triggered ability on the chain with effect {type:'draw', amount:1}, optional:false. After the player passed priority (step 38) it resolved and player-1 drew a card (hand went 4 -> 5, 'Plundering Poro' appeared).
findings.why_wrong: Patched Porobot reads 'When you play me, if you control 3 or more other gear, draw 1.' Per rule 383.2.a.1, an 'if' clause immediately after the trigger condition is part of the Trigger Condition; with 0 gear controlled the condition is not fulfilled and the ability must not be placed on the chain at all, let alone resolve into a draw. The chain item carries no condition and the card's parsed ability (ven.json abilities: [null], generated from rulesText) evidently dropped the 'control 3+ other gear' gate, giving a free card.
findings.reason: Bug confirmed, though the mechanism differs slightly from the claim. The parser does NOT drop the gate: enrichCard re-parses rulesText (all-cards.ts:805-807 leaves abilities undefined when set JSON has [null]) and yields a triggered ability with condition {type:"control", target:{type:"gear", controller:"friendly", quantity:{atLeast:3}}} (verified by running getCardRegistry().get("ven-058-166")). The engine drops it: trigger-runner.ts:110-130 evaluateTriggerCondition only handles "legion" and "paid-additional-cost" and falls through to `return true` (line 129) for any other condition type, so the "control 3+ gear" condition is treated as satisfied. fireTriggers then pushes the bare effect {type:'draw',amount:1} onto the chain with no condition (trigger-runner.ts:317-335), matching the trace chain item exactly. Rule 383.2.a.1 confirms the 'if' clause is part of the trigger condition, so with 0 gear the ability should never be chained.

findings.why_wrong: DESIGN.md: 'Legend/Champion always visible for both players' and 'All deck card images preloaded at first sync — no blank cards after t+1s'. Rules 111/112: each player's Champion Legend and Chosen Champion are in the Legend/Champion zones from game start (public zones, 355.10.a.1). A human sees 'I have no legend or champion' on turn 1.
findings.reason: Screenshots 02.png and 03.png both show player-1 LEGEND/CHAMPION slots, both rune cards, Aspirant's Climb battlefield, and 2 of 4 opponent hand cards as empty frames while engine state has those cards; 04.png shows them all loaded — a pure image-load latency gap past DESIGN.md:30's "no blank cards after t+1s" budget (and DESIGN.md:13 legend/champion always visible). Source mechanism: (1) apps/riftbound-app/public/js/gameplay/renderer.js:680-681 renders `` with the `.card-fallback` (name/cost) only revealed via `onerror` — public/css sets `.card .card-fallback {display:none}` (line 386-387) — so a still-loading image is an empty frame with no interim content. (2) apps/riftbound-app/server.ts:2384-2401: downloads/card-images/ does not exist in this checkout (verified), so every /card-image/:id request 302-redirects to the external CDN URL (cardImageUrls), adding a cross-origin round trip per card. (3) public/js/gameplay/websocket.js:57 (preloadCardImages, lines 7-19) only fires `new Image().src` on the first `sync` message — the same tick as the first render() at line 65 — so the "preload" gives zero head start for cards visible on the opening board. findings.reason: Screenshots 00.png/03.png confirm player-1 (dev, order/mind saved deck: 35 main+5 hand, 10+2 runes) has empty Legend and Champion zones from game start while Goldfish (default fury/chaos deck) has both. Source: the lobby start path (server.ts:2794 loadDeckConfig(lobby.host.deckId)) -> savedDeckToDeckConfig (server.ts:881-929) only rejects decks with empty main/rune (897-905) and returns legendId/championId as undefined when the saved deck has none; createGameFromDecks then guards placement with `if (deck.legendId)` (server.ts:1027) and `if (deck.championId)` (server.ts:1044), silently skipping placeLegend/placeChampion and proceeding to shuffle/draw. select_deck (server.ts:2714-2716) also performs no legality check. So the server starts a game without a Champion Legend/Chosen Champion, violating rules 103.1.a/111/112 setup requirements. It is a server/setup bug rather than a UI render failure.

findings.what: Clicking 'Play Spell — Bellows Breath' immediately put the spell on the chain with targets=[player's own Recruit token] (the only enumerated playSpell move had that target pre-filled). The player was never asked to choose targets, and could not choose zero targets or decline hitting their own 1-Might Recruit, which will now die on resolution.
findings.why_wrong: Bellows Breath reads 'Deal 1 to up to three units at the same location.' Per rule 355.13, for 'up to N' the controller chooses any number of available targets including zero; target choice belongs to the player at play time (355). Auto-selecting the caster's own unit with no targeting prompt removes a mandatory player choice and forces self-damage.
findings.reason: Engine enumerator packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/cards.ts:1378-1416 handles any caster-chosen card target (including quantity {upTo:3}) by pushing exactly one variant per single valid target (`targets: [targetId]`, line 1410-1414); it never emits a zero-target variant nor multi-target subsets for "up to N" (only the split-damage refTgt path uses enumerateSubsetsUpTo). With the own Recruit as the sole unit, the only playSpell move is targets=[Recruit] (matches trace step 27 moves list). UI apps/riftbound-app/public/js/gameplay/renderer.js:1072-1075: when a moveId group has exactly one move, the action button's onclick is `executeMove(moveId, m.params, ...)` with the pre-filled params — no targeting prompt; and renderer.js:297 labels playSpell with only the card name, hiding the target. Trace step 28 shows the chain item with targets=[token-recruit...] immediately after the click. Rule 355.13 confirms 'up to' allows choosing zero targets.

findings.what: Picked card is drawn to hand instead of banished and played at cost reduced by 5

findings.observed: pendingChoice was {type:'reveal-and-pick', onPicked:'draw', onRest:'recycle'}; UI title 'Choose a card to draw'. After picking, Legion Rearguard went to hand; base empty, banishment empty, energy unchanged (4).
findings.reason: reinforce.ts has no abilities, so rulesText is parsed. parseLookEffect (packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/index.ts:1851-1858) matches only the "Look at the top 5 cards of your Main Deck." prefix and returns {amount:5, from:"deck", type:"look"} — verified by running parseAbilities on the exact rulesText; the "banish a unit … then play it, reducing its cost by [5]" clause is dropped. The executor (packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effect-executor.ts:1415-1416) treats a bare look (no `then`) as Stacked-Deck shape: onPicked defaults to "draw", onRest to "recycle". This matches the observed pendingChoice {onPicked:'draw', onRest:'recycle'} and the picked card going to hand with no banish/play/cost reduction.

findings.reason: Reinforce (riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogn/reinforce.ts) has no hand-authored abilities, so enrich-cards.ts:29 runs parseAbilities on its rulesText, which yields only `{type:"look", amount:5, from:"deck"}` — the "banish a unit from among them" clause is dropped (verified by running the parser). In riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effect-executor.ts:1396-1431 the "look" case builds pendingChoice = {type:"reveal-and-pick", revealed: topN, onPicked:"draw", onRest:"recycle"} with no `filter` field (lines 1420-1430). pending-choice.ts:37 only restricts picks via choice.filter?.excludeCardTypes, which is absent here, so resolvePendingChoice is enumerable for all 5 revealed cards including spells.

findings.what: No way to decline the optional pick
findings.expected: "You may banish a unit" - player should be able to pick nothing and just recycle all 5.

findings.reason: Reinforce (ogn-062-298) enriches at runtime to a bare `{type:"look", amount:5, from:"deck"}` (verified via bun getCardRegistry(); parseLookEffect at riftbound-cards/src/parser/index.ts:1851-1858 drops the "You may banish a unit…" clause). In effect-executor.ts `case "look"` (1396-1431), `visionLike = lookEff.then?.recycle !== undefined` is false for this shape, so the pendingChoice is built with onPicked="draw", onRest="recycle" and `optional` is only spread when visionLike (line 1425) — i.e. NOT set for Reinforce. In pending-choice.ts the reveal-and-pick enumerator only appends `{accept:false}` when `choice.optional` (lines 222-226) and the condition only permits accept:false when `choice.optional` (line 146). Hence only pickedCardId moves are legal/enumerated; there is no decline path that recycles all 5. Bug confirmed in engine layer.

findings.what: 'If it would die this turn, banish it instead' replacement not applied
findings.expected: Legion Rearguard (2 Might) taking 3 damage from Smite should be banished (go to banishment zone) instead of dying normally
findings.observed: Rearguard was killed and moved to trash (trash=[Smite, Rearguard], banishment=[]). Chain item effect was only {type:damage, amount:3}; runtime-parsed ability has no banish-instead clause.
findings.reason: Smite (unl-007-219) card def at packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/smite.ts:4-16 has no `abilities`, so the runtime parser is used. Running parseAbilities on its rulesText returns only [{type:"spell", timing:"action", effect:{type:"damage", amount:3, target:{type:"unit", location:"battlefield"}}}] — the "If it would die this turn, banish it instead." sentence is silently dropped. parseReplacementAbility (packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/index.ts:4890-4930) only matches "The next time X would die..." / "EFFECT the next time it..." forms, not the "If it would die this turn, banish it instead" rider following a damage effect. Hence no die->banish replacement is registered and the killed Rearguard goes to trash.

findings.what: Smite card moved to trash before it resolved
findings.expected: Spell sits on the chain until it resolves, then goes to trash
findings.observed: Immediately after playSpell (chain item still pending, priority not passed) zones.trash already contained player-1-main-999-unl-007-219 and zones.chain was empty
findings.reason: playSpell reducer (packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/cards.ts:1576-1601) adds the chain item to draft.interaction via addToChain and then immediately calls zones.moveCard({cardId, targetZoneId: "trash"}) (line 1598-1601, comment "Move spell to trash (it resolves from the chain later)"). The "chain" zone is defined (src/zones/zone-configs.ts:145-148) but never used for spells, and chain-moves.ts has no trash move on spell resolution — so the card physically sits in trash for the entire time its chain item is pending. Rules text says the spell's effect is executed "and then place the card in the Trash of the owning player", and countered items "cleared from the chain ... are placed in the trash", i.e. trash placement happens at resolution, not at play. Generic engine issue (not Smite-specific); observable e.g. via trash-targeting/Flow effects while the spell is still on the chain.

findings.what: 'At the start of your Beginning Phase, recycle 3 from your trash' never fires

The engine never emits a matching event: the beginning phase onBegin in packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/flow/riftbound-flow.ts:241-321 only kills Temporary permanents, scores, and fires "hold" (line 318); no "beginning-phase" (nor "start-of-turn") event is fired anywhere in riftbound-engine/src outside tests (game-events.ts:26 declares start-of-turn but grep finds no emitter). trigger-matcher.ts:161 falls back to event.type so the EVENT_MAP omission itself isn't the blocker, but since no beginning-phase event is ever dispatched, Dr. Mundo's recycle-3 trigger can never fire.

findings.what: Shield 2 does not increase Mutated Mouser's own Might for lethal-damage/kill determination while defending
findings.expected: Per rulesText/[814.1.c] Mouser is a 3-Might unit while defender. Defending (with a friendly 2-Might Legion Rearguard) against a lone 2-Might attacker, Tank forces both damage onto Mouser, 2 < 3 so Mouser survives and Rearguard takes 0.
findings.observed: After resolveFullCombat Mouser was killed (sent to trash) and the friendly Legion Rearguard took 1 overflow damage — i.e. Mouser was treated as 1 Might (lethal=1). combat-resolver distributeDamage/kill check use baseMight only; Shield is only added to the side's outgoing damage total.
findings.reason: combat-resolver.ts:80 adds Shield only to the defending side's outgoing damage total (calculateSideMight). distributeDamage computes lethal as `unit.baseMight - unit.currentDamage` (combat-resolver.ts:114) and the kill check is `totalDamage >= unit.baseMight` (combat-resolver.ts:171), with baseMight = def.might (moves/combat.ts:320,354). So Mutated Mouser (might 1, Shield 2, Tank) is treated as 1-Might for lethal/kill while defending: a 2-Might attacker assigns 1 lethal to Mouser (killed) and 1 overflows to Legion Rearguard, matching the observed behavior.

findings.what: No target selection for 'Choose a friendly unit and an enemy unit'

findings.observed: With two friendly Legion Rearguards and one enemy unit on board, no prompt/pendingChoice or per-target playSpell moves were offered; on resolution the engine silently picked the first friendly unit (player-1-main-3).

Then effect-executor.ts:1333-1364 `case "fight"` calls resolveTarget on attacker/defender descriptors and uses attackers[0]/defenders[0], never consulting ctx.boundTargets (contrast swap-might at effect-executor.ts:903-913 which does). But picking the Abandoned Hall battlefield fails: 'Move rejected: Target zone battlefield-battlefield-player-1-bf-unl-205-219 does not exist' (EXECUTION_ERROR). effect-executor.ts 'move'/to:'choose' emits options already prefixed 'battlefield-<bfId>' while resolvePendingChoice (pending-choice.ts ~L367) prefixes 'battlefield-' again. findings.expected: At end of P1's turn, P1's Dazzling Aurora triggers, reveals Akshan (top of deck), banishes and plays him; Akshan's play effect (with [body][body] paid) takes control of the enemy Dazzling Aurora, which should NOT trigger that same turn (only on P1's future turns).
findings.observed: P1's own Dazzling Aurora never triggered at end of turn. Setup: P1 Aurora played to base (playGear), P2 Aurora placed in P2 base (duplicateCard), Akshan placed on top of P1 deck (placeCardsOnTopOfDeckInOrder), body x2 + energy added, then endTurn. Result: flow cascaded straight to P1 turn 3; banishment empty, no chain item, no reveal; Akshan was simply drawn into hand by the turn-3 draw step (hand 5->6, deck top shifted by exactly one). Enemy Aurora stayed under P2 control. The ruling's premise (Aurora playing Akshan at end of turn) cannot occur, so the trigger-timing question is unreachable.
findings.notes: Root cause (from local source, packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/flow/riftbound-flow.ts): the ending phase onBegin only clears damage/stun/might mods and empties rune pools; nothing in the flow (or server) ever calls fireTriggers({type:'end-of-turn'}) — the only flow-fired triggers are 'ready' and 'hold'. 'end-of-turn'/'start-of-turn' exist in game-events.ts/trigger-matcher.ts and are exercised only by unit tests that fire the event manually. Secondary concerns even once fixed: (a) ending.onBegin empties rune pools before any end-of-turn trigger could resolve, so Akshan's optional [body][body] cost could never be paid from floating power; (b) the reveal handler plays the hit via a chain 'move to choose' item rather than the playUnit path, so paidAdditionalCost/optional-cost prompting for Akshan likely wouldn't be offered. Screenshots: /tmp/ruling-56312d623221a2f8-pre.png (board before endTurn), /tmp/ruling-56312d623221a2f8.png (after).

Root causes: packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser drops the control-duration sentence for Akshan; packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effect-executor.ts case 'take-control' is unimplemented; 'move to base' on a gear already in the shared base zone does not alter controller.

findings.expected: Per ruling (and rule 355.2.a), Astral Heron can be played directly to a battlefield its controller controls; if it is the first card played that turn, its own 'When you play your first card each turn, if I'm at a battlefield' trigger should fire after it resolves at the battlefield.
